     2	======================================
     3	
     4	1. Introduction
     5	
     6	   KVP is a simple text-based protocol for an in-memory key-value store.
     7	   Commands are line-oriented. Each command is a single line of text.
     8	   Responses follow a structured format described below.
     9	
    10	2. Commands
    11	
    12	   2.1 SET <key> <value>
    13	       Store the given value under the given key.
    14	       Response: OK
    15	       Errors: ERR key_too_long (if key exceeds 64 chars)
    16	               ERR value_too_large (if value exceeds 1024 chars)
    17	               ERR store_full (if store has 100 keys and key is new)
    18	
    19	   2.2 GET <key>
    20	       Retrieve the value stored under the given key.
    21	       Response: the value on a single line
    22	       Errors: ERR key_not_found
    23	
    24	   2.3 DEL <key>
    25	       Remove the given key from the store.
    26	       Response: OK
    27	       Errors: ERR key_not_found
    28	
    29	   2.4 KEYS
    30	       List all stored keys.
    31	       Response: one key per line, terminated by END
    32	
    33	   2.5 COUNT
    34	       Return the number of stored keys.
    35	       Response: COUNT <n>
    36	
    37	   2.6 EXISTS <key>
    38	       Check if a key exists.
    39	       Response: TRUE or FALSE
    40	
    41	   2.7 FLUSH
    42	       Remove all keys.
    43	       Response: OK
    44	
    45	   2.8 MSET <key1> <value1> <key2> <value2> ...
    46	       Set multiple key-value pairs atomically.
    47	       Response: OK <n> (where n = number of pairs set)
    48	
    49	   2.9 MGET <key1> <key2> ...
    50	       Get multiple values.
    51	       Response: value or NIL per key, one per line, terminated by END
    52	
    53	   2.10 SETEX <key> <seconds> <value>

    57	
    58	   2.11 TTL <key>
